requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

[mp-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30408133/mp-repro.zip)

story.summary: Stops `TypeCollector` from indexing `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` in two diagnostic paths: line 985 now uses a new `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` helper and line 1077 uses `FirstOrDefault()`. It also wraps every analyzer diagnostic report in a filter that drops any diagnostic whose location is not a syntax tree of the current compilation. Three tests compile a defining library to metadata and use its closed generic struct or record struct as a member type. README and the MsgPack004 doc gain notes saying diagnostics for referenced-assembly types belong to the defining project.
story.why: When a closed generic value type comes from a referenced assembly, `GetObjectInfo` runs on a symbol with no syntax. The `[0]` indexing then throws, the generator contributes nothing, and the app ships with no resolver.
touches_beyond_requirement: A blanket filter on all analyzer diagnostics (line 239, lines 1444-1450). It silently drops any diagnostic without an in-compilation source location, not only those for metadata types.
Two user-facing docs (README, MsgPack004.md) that state a new policy: diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are reported only by the defining project.
story.confidence_overview: Medium. The two changed indexing sites are clearly safe now. However, the issue names three sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101); the diff touches only two, roughly 25 lines below the old 1009 and 1101, so the third (~735) looks untouched. The verifier part of the tests plausibly catches CS8785/AD0001. The second half of the test helper asserts nothing useful, and its `expectedResolverHintName` parameter is never used. The line-985 change has no test.

claims.text: RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync runs the source-generator verifier with the defining assembly added only as an AdditionalReference, with the generated-source snapshot check skipped. It relies on the verifier failing on any unexpected diagnostic, such as CS8785 or AD0001.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

breaker.reason: In GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 628-648, the requirement ('A clean build, with a generated resolver in app.') is only partly met and lines 631 and 633 in the cited range are contradicted: line 631 documents that RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync verifies 'that the resolver named expectedResolverHintName is generated', yet line 641 sets TestBehaviors = TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck (and lines 650-659 ignore expectedResolverHintName), so none of the three named tests verifies that a resolver is generated. Furthermore, CS8785 has DiagnosticSeverity.Warning (unlike AD0001, which is an analyzer diagnostic), and Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing defaults SourceGeneratorTest.CompilerDiagnostics to CompilerDiagnostics.Errors; with SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck enabled at line 641, VerifyCS.Test will ignore CS8785 unless CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier (not shown in the diff) overrides CompilerDiagnostics to include warnings.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic uses a new helper `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation`, which returns null when the property has no source declaration. Because it uses an `as` cast, it also returns null rather than throwing when the declaring syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs line 985 and lines 1429-1434: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull calls GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item), which uses FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax and returns null both when DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty and when the declaring syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax.

breaker.reason: Checked README.md lines 1639-1643: adds the 'Generic types from referenced assemblies' subsection stating closed generic types (including generic value types and record structs) from referenced assemblies can be used as members of [MessagePackObject] types and that member diagnostics are reported by the defining assembly.

claims.text: MsgPack004 doc gains a section stating the analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.

breaker.reason: Checked doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md lines 48-52: adds the 'Types from referenced assemblies' section stating the analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled and that members of types from referenced assemblies are reported by their defining project.

claims.text: The analyzer's report callback is wrapped so a diagnostic is reported only when its Location is in source and its SourceTree belongs to the current compilation. Otherwise it is silently dropped. A null report callback stays null.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs line 239 and lines 1436-1450: when reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null, this.reportDiagnostic stays null; otherwise it delegates to ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which only invokes report(diagnostic) when diagnostic.Location.IsInSource and this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree) are both true. ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember exercises dropping a metadata member diagnostic.

claims.text: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic now gets its location via `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()`, so an unkeyed public member of a metadata type no longer throws IndexOutOfRangeException. The resulting location-less diagnostic is then dropped by the C1 filter.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs line 1077: MemberNeedsKey now resolves its location via item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), avoiding IndexOutOfRangeException when DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty on metadata members and producing Location.None, which ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops when invoked at line 1080. Tested by ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember.

findings.description: Claim C7 disputed: In GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 628-648, the requirement ('A clean build, with a generated resolver in app.') is only partly met and lines 631 and 633 in the cited range are contradicted: line 631 documents that RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync verifies 'that the resolver named expectedResolverHintName is generated', yet line 641 sets TestBehaviors = TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck (and lines 650-659 ignore expectedResolverHintName), so none of the three named tests verifies that a resolver is generated. Furthermore, CS8785 has DiagnosticSeverity.Warning (unlike AD0001, which is an analyzer diagnostic), and Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Testing defaults SourceGeneratorTest.CompilerDiagnostics to CompilerDiagnostics.Errors; with SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck enabled at line 641, VerifyCS.Test will ignore CS8785 unless CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier (not shown in the diff) overrides CompilerDiagnostics to include warnings.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). The changed sites sit about 25 lines below the old 1009 and 1101, so the third site (~old 735, ~new 710) appears unchanged. If that path fires for some metadata types, the crash remains. No test shows which path the record-struct repro actually hits.

The filter drops every diagnostic without an in-compilation source location, including ones for source types whose location helper returned null (for example GetIdentifierLocation casts that yield null) or any diagnostic intentionally reported at Location.None. Legitimate warnings can disappear silently; this hides problems rather than fixing their location.

`Assert.NotNull(hintNames)` can never fail, and `expectedResolverHintName` is unused. The 'resolver was actually generated' check the comment promises does not exist. Assert.Empty only looks at Error severity, while CS8785 is a warning.
The changed BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path has no test exercising it with a metadata type.

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation uses 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax', which returns null for positional record and record struct properties declared in source in the current compilation (e.g., 'public record Cmd([property: Key((string?)null!)] string Scope)'), because Roslyn's DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax() for a positional record property is ParameterSyntax, not PropertyDeclarationSyntax. That gives BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (line 985) Location.None, causing ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (line 1446) to silently drop the diagnostic on user code in the current compilation.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filters diagnostics by diagnostic.Location.IsInSource rather than checking whether the analyzed type belongs to this.compilation.Assembly. Consequently, any Location.None diagnostic legitimately produced for a type in the current compilation (for instance via GetParameterListLocation at line 1454 when method is null or an implicitly declared constructor with empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences, or GetIdentifierLocation at line 1427 on non-BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax symbols) is now silently swallowed instead of reported.

Immediately above the fixed MemberNeedsKey branch on line 1077, the AOTDerivedKeyAttribute branch still calls derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation() unconditionally (even in MessagePackGenerator where reportDiagnostic is null and before line 1078 checks accessibility). If a closed generic value type in a referenced assembly has a member annotated with an attribute deriving from KeyAttribute, ApplicationSyntaxReference is null in metadata and line 1076 will throw NullReferenceException, crashing both the generator (CS8785, omitting the resolver) and the analyzer (AD0001).
